# RecDiffy.NET profiles: diff and tolerances

> After matching, every Key and Economic field of a matched entry is compared. Decimals are rounded to the field's scale first, then judged against the tolerance, which is inclusive. A compared field with no tolerance is compared exactly. Null against a value is a Break: missing isn't zero. Up: https://m-vaysman.github.io/recdiffy.net/docs/profiles/llms.txt

## Reference

- [Diff](https://m-vaysman.github.io/recdiffy.net/docs/reference/profiles/diff.md): absolute, relative, days and attributed tolerances, when, applicableWhen, and which kind fits which type
- [How a field is compared](https://m-vaysman.github.io/recdiffy.net/docs/reference/results/how-a-field-is-compared.md): rounding first, then the inclusive bound
- [Grouped entries](https://m-vaysman.github.io/recdiffy.net/docs/reference/results/grouped-entries.md): how a many-to-one match is compared
- [Attributions](https://m-vaysman.github.io/recdiffy.net/docs/reference/profiles/attributions.md): trading.netCash and trading.proRataToQuantity
- [Attributed differences in the result](https://m-vaysman.github.io/recdiffy.net/docs/reference/results/attributed-differences.md): FieldDiff.AttributedTo
- [Missing isn't zero](https://m-vaysman.github.io/recdiffy.net/docs/reference/results/missing-isnt-zero.md): nulls in comparison, and why to check IsNull before Delta
